# Verification & Tooling Checklist: Repository Foundation (Stage 0)

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the verification command, reproducibility, and quality-gate requirements (FR-001–FR-011, SC-001–SC-008) in the Repository Foundation spec.
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Feature**: [specs/001-repository-foundation/spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Verification Command (FR-001–FR-004)

- [ ] CHK001 Does FR-001's "single documented command" name the authoritative location where it is documented (e.g., a README section), or is "documented" left ambiguous? [Clarity, FR-001/FR-014]
- [ ] CHK002 Is check composition inside the command (execution order, short-circuit-on-failure, exit-status semantics) specified at the requirements level, or only in implementation artifacts (`contracts/verification.md`, research D1)? [Gap, FR-001]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the passing/failing contract of FR-002 defined in observable terms (process exit status), or merely as "result"? [Clarity, FR-002]
- [ ] CHK004 Is SC-002's "<60 s per run" bound an owned, testable requirement, or is it a success-criteria metric with no owning FR to enforce it? [Coverage, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK005 Is "meaningful check" (FR-003) given an objective definition consistent with SC-003's "substantive check", or do two different terms describe the same requirement? [Ambiguity, FR-003/SC-003]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the FR-004 default-state guarantee consistent with the empty-run guard in Edge Cases — i.e., is it clear that a default passing only because nothing is verified does NOT satisfy FR-004? [Consistency, FR-004/Edge Cases]

## Reproducibility & Manifest (FR-005–FR-008)

- [ ] CHK007 Is FR-005 unambiguous about which file is the "version-controlled manifest" (`pyproject.toml`) versus the resolved lock output (`uv.lock`), consistent with the assumption that the lock is an output, not an input? [Clarity, FR-005/Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "yield the same result" (FR-006) normalized to the objective standard in SC-004 (identical tooling versions between machines), or does the spec state two different reproducibility standards? [Consistency, FR-006/SC-004]
- [ ] CHK009 Are requirements specified for checking lockfile reproducibility itself (lock verification/resolution equivalence), or only for the outcome? [Gap, FR-006]
- [ ] CHK010 Does FR-007 define the content of an "actionable message" (minimum runtime, installed runtime, remediation step) or leave it to the implementer? [Clarity, FR-007/SC-007]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the offline edge case (verification against an already-prepared environment with no network) expressed as an explicit requirement, or only in Edge Cases? [Gap, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the partial-prep-failure visibility requirement (environment prepared partway must not appear healthy) enforceable by an owning FR, or does it live only in Edge Cases? [Gap, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK013 Is SC-001's "under 10 minutes" bound measurable as stated (objective timing), and is the prerequisite set it depends on ("git", "uv") explicitly bounded? [Measurability, SC-001]

## Quality Gates (FR-009–FR-011)

- [ ] CHK014 Does FR-009 define what counts as a "class of defect" distinctly, and is it consistent between the tool-agnostic requirement text and the tool-named assumptions (linter + type checker)? [Consistency, FR-009/Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the "verification remains the final authority when gates are bypassed" property (US3 scenario 3, Edge Cases) stated as an explicit requirement, or only as an acceptance scenario? [Gap, FR-011]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the requirements layer require identification of the offending location on failure (FR-011) consistent with SC-006's 100% locator bound, or is location reporting missing from requirements? [Completeness, FR-011/SC-006]
- [ ] CHK017 Is FR-010 unambiguous about the authority hierarchy when a contributor-local override conflicts with version-controlled gate configuration? [Clarity, FR-010]
- [ ] CHK018 Are SC-005/SC-006's "10 seeded defects, 100% of trials" criteria defined with a representative defect set, or is the trial methodology unspecified? [Measurability, SC-005/SC-006]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK019 Are all four US1 acceptance scenarios measurable Given/When/Then statements with a single unambiguous success signal (exit code vs output text) each? [Measurability, US1 AS1–AS4]
- [ ] CHK020 Do SC-001–SC-010 each trace to at least one FR, or do some success criteria (e.g., survey-based SC-008) lack an owning requirement? [Traceability, SC-001–SC-010]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the "intentionally stale or unsupported runtime" test premise (SC-007) concrete enough to reproduce — is a specific version strategy named for simulating the mismatch? [Clarity, SC-007]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK022 Are recovery/rollback concerns intentionally excluded (no state mutation at Stage 0) in an explicit Out-of-Scope statement, rather than silently absent? [Recovery, Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the cold-checkout scenario (US1 AS1) covered consistently across the requirement (FR-008), the success criterion (SC-001), and the runnable steps (`quickstart.md` §3.1)? [Coverage, US1 AS1/FR-008/SC-001]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the empty-suite guard consistent between FR-003, the Edge Cases entry, `quickstart.md` §3.3, and tasks T013/T016 — same definition of a non-real pass? [Consistency, FR-003/Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the secrets edge case consistent between the requirement (FR-015), US2 scenario 4, and `quickstart.md` §3.7 — same definition of what must be excluded and what template must exist? [Consistency, FR-015/US2 AS4]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK026 Is the toolchain-assumption conflict resolved: Assumptions name `Pydantic`/`SQLAlchemy`/`Alembic` while research D3 and `implementation-plan.md` §4 disagree on whether Stage 0 configures them — is the implementer left with a contradiction? [Conflict, Assumptions/research D3]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the external prerequisite `uv` (and `git`) declared as part of FR-008, or is it an implicit assumption the spec never states? [Assumption, FR-008/SC-001]
- [ ] CHK028 Given the assumption that `docker-compose.yml` is provisioned but not exercised, is it defined whether the file must at least validate (e.g., `docker compose config`) within verification, or is that ambiguity? [Consistency, Assumption docker-compose]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK029 Does the spec resolve what counts as "prior project knowledge" between FR-008 (no prior knowledge) and SC-001 (bounded prerequisites), without ambiguity about what a contributor must already know? [Ambiguity, FR-008/SC-001]
- [ ] CHK030 Are "automated verification", "quality gates", and "verification command" used as consistently defined terms across FR-001, FR-009, FR-011, and Key Entities, or do overlapping terms risk scope confusion? [Consistency, FR-001/FR-009/Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the boundary between the single verify command (FR-001) and the documented setup step ("make env" in `quickstart.md`/README) explicitly stated, so "one command" cannot be read as "no setup step"? [Ambiguity, FR-001/FR-008/quickstart §3.1]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`
- This checklist tests the REQUIREMENTS (FR-001–FR-011 + SC + Edge Cases), not the implementation; prior knowledge of `tasks.md`/`research.md` is used only to detect requirement-level gaps
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
